markets.title: US 10-year Treasury yields risk hitting 6% for first time since 2000, Pimco says
markets.raw_summary: Bond giant’s investment chief warns that further sharp rise in borrowing costs is ‘feasible’ as market participants are forced to unwind losing bets

insight.what: 品浩首席投资官警告，10年期美国国债收益率可能升破6%，为2000年以来首次，因杠杆投资者被迫抛售亏损债券。
insight.why: 市场原本以为10年期美债收益率已在4%附近见顶，这一警告把长端利率的定价中枢上移，全球风险资产的估值分母都被重估。
insight.chain: 对冲基金债券持仓亏损 → 被迫平仓卖出 → 长端美债卖压加大 → 10年期收益率上行 → 全球资产折现率抬升 → 高估值与长久期资产承压；同时美债收益率抬升 → 美元资产吸引力上升 → 新兴市场资本外流压力加大
notes: 为什么10年期美债收益率重要？它是全球资产定价的基准无风险利率 Rf，其他资产（股票、公司债、海外债）都在它之上加一层风险溢价来定价。
债券价格和收益率呈反向变动：收益率上升，存量债券价格下跌，谁手里拿着债谁就账面亏损。
什么是杠杆投资者被迫平仓？对冲基金常用借来的钱买债，债券价格一跌，抵押品价值缩水，券商要求追加保证金，基金只能被迫卖出，进一步压低价格，形成负反馈。
收益率破6%意味着什么？意味着美国政府的长期借贷成本回到2000年水平，房贷、企业贷、股票折现率都会同步往上抬。
折现率抬升为什么伤害成长股？成长股的大部分利润在未来，未来利润折回今天要除以一个利率因子，利率越高，折回后的现值越小。
为什么美元会走强？美债收益率高，全球资金愿意换美元买美债，美元需求上升，汇率走强，反过来压制新兴市场货币和资产。

insight_en.what: PIMCO's chief investment officer warned that the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield could rise above 6% for the first time since 2000 as leveraged investors are forced to sell bonds at a loss.
insight_en.why: The market had thought that the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield had already peaked near 4%. This warning shifts the pricing anchor for long-term interest rates upward, repricing the valuation denominators of all global risk assets.
insight_en.chain: Losses on hedge funds' bond holdings → Forced liquidation and selling → Increased selling pressure on long-dated U.S. Treasuries → Higher 10-year Treasury yield → Higher discount rates for global assets → Pressure on high-valuation and long-duration assets；At the same time, higher U.S. Treasury yields → Greater appeal of dollar-denominated assets → Increased capital outflow pressure on emerging markets
notes: Why does the 10-year U.S. Treasury yield matter? It is the benchmark risk-free rate Rf for global asset pricing; other assets (stocks, corporate bonds, and overseas bonds) are priced by adding a risk premium on top of it.
Bond prices and yields move inversely: when yields rise, the prices of outstanding bonds fall, and anyone holding those bonds incurs unrealized losses.

What does forced liquidation mean for leveraged investors? Hedge funds often use borrowed money to buy bonds. When bond prices fall, collateral values shrink, brokers demand additional margin, and funds have no choice but to sell, pushing prices down further and creating a negative feedback loop.

What does a yield above 6% mean? It means the U.S. government's long-term borrowing costs return to their 2000 level, with mortgage rates, corporate lending rates, and equity discount rates all rising in tandem.

Why do higher discount rates hurt growth stocks? Most of growth stocks' earnings come in the future. Discounting future earnings back to today requires dividing by an interest rate factor; the higher the interest rate, the lower the resulting present value.

Why would the dollar strengthen? Higher U.S. Treasury yields make global investors willing to convert funds into dollars to buy U.S. Treasuries, increasing demand for dollars and strengthening the exchange rate, which in turn weighs on emerging-market currencies and assets.

markets.title: Inflation on many everyday items was entirely due to tariffs, NY Fed says
markets.raw_summary: Tariffs added 2.9 percentage points to inflation in 67 categories of goods by February 2026, researchers at the New York Federal Reserve found.

insight.what: 纽约联储研究显示，截至2026年2月，关税已推动67类商品价格上涨，累计贡献2.9个百分点的通胀。
insight.why: 市场此前认为关税主要是一次性价格冲击、不影响长期通胀预期，这份研究把它坐实为持续通胀来源，压缩了美联储降息空间。
insight.chain: 关税落地 → 进口商成本上升 → 转嫁给消费者 → 核心商品通胀黏性上升 → 美联储降息推迟 → 短端美债收益率维持高位 → 美元偏强、成长股承压
notes: 什么是核心通胀？剔除食品和能源后的通胀，美联储更看重它，因为它反映的是趋势性价格压力。
为什么关税会推高通胀？进口商品被加税，进口商要么自己承担利润缩水，要么把成本加到售价上，后者就推高物价。
为什么这份研究关键？它用数据把关税和2.9个百分点的涨价直接挂钩，打破了'关税只是短暂冲击'的假设。
降息推迟意味着什么？市场原本押注美联储很快降息，现在预期落空，短端国债收益率下不去，美元保持强势。
传导到股票：无风险利率不降，股票折现率就降不下来，高估值的科技成长股对利率最敏感，承压最大。

insight_en.what: Research by the Federal Reserve Bank of New York shows that, as of February 2026, tariffs had pushed up prices in 67 categories of goods, cumulatively contributing 2.9 percentage points to inflation.
insight_en.why: The market had previously viewed tariffs mainly as a one-off price shock that would not affect long-term inflation expectations. This research establishes them as a persistent source of inflation, reducing the Federal Reserve's room to cut interest rates.
insight_en.chain: Tariffs take effect → Importers' costs rise → Costs are passed on to consumers → Core goods inflation becomes stickier → Federal Reserve rate cuts are delayed → Short-term U.S. Treasury yields remain elevated → Dollar stays firm, growth stocks come under pressure
notes: What is core inflation? Inflation excluding food and energy. The Federal Reserve places more weight on it because it reflects underlying price pressures.
Why do tariffs push up inflation? Imported goods are taxed, and importers must either absorb the hit to profits themselves or add the costs to selling prices; the latter pushes up prices.
Why is this research crucial? It uses data to directly link tariffs to a 2.9-percentage-point increase in prices, overturning the assumption that 'tariffs are only a temporary shock.'

What do delayed rate cuts mean? The market had been betting that the Federal Reserve would cut rates soon, but those expectations have now been disappointed, leaving short-term Treasury yields unable to fall and the dollar strong.

Transmission to equities: if the risk-free rate does not fall, equity discount rates cannot fall either. Highly valued technology growth stocks are the most sensitive to interest rates and face the greatest pressure.

policy.title: Can China use its widening US yield gap to boost the yuan’s global role?
policy.raw_summary: China should seize a window opened by the widening US-China yield gap to strengthen the financing, hedging and asset-absorption systems behind the yuan, turning its cyclical low-interest-rate advantag

insight.what: 南华早报提出，中国应抓住中美利差扩大的窗口，完善人民币融资、对冲和资产吸纳体系，推动人民币国际化。
insight.why: 市场原本认为中美利差倒挂只会加剧人民币贬值压力，这篇观点把它重新解读为低成本融资窗口，改变了跨境资金流的叙事。
insight.chain: 中美利差扩大 → 离岸人民币融资成本低于美元 → 境外主体借人民币意愿上升 → 人民币跨境使用增加 → 人民币国际需求上升 → 对汇率形成一定支撑；但若利差持续倒挂 → 套利资金反向流动 → 短期贬值压力仍在
notes: 什么是中美利差？中国国债收益率和美国国债收益率的差，利差倒挂指中国收益率低于美国，历史上会吸引资金流向美元资产。
为什么利差扩大还能利好人民币？因为融资成本低的人民币可以成为套利货币，境外机构借人民币换成美元投资，这个过程本身需要先买入人民币。
什么是资产吸纳体系？指让境外持有的人民币有地方投资，比如人民币债券、股票、理财产品，否则别人拿了人民币也只能换回美元。
为什么对冲体系重要？境外机构持有人民币资产怕汇率波动，需要外汇衍生品来对冲，市场深度不够他们就不敢长期持有。
这条逻辑成立的条件：资本账户开放程度、人民币资产回报率、汇率预期稳定性，三者缺一不可。

insight_en.what: The South China Morning Post argued that China should seize the window created by the widening China-U.S. interest rate differential to improve its renminbi financing, hedging, and asset absorption framework and promote renminbi internationalization.
insight_en.why: The market had thought that a negative China-U.S. interest rate differential would only intensify depreciation pressure on the renminbi. This commentary reinterprets it as a window for low-cost financing, changing the narrative around cross-border capital flows.
insight_en.chain: Widening China-U.S. interest rate differential → Offshore renminbi funding costs lower than dollar funding costs → Greater willingness among offshore entities to borrow renminbi → Increased cross-border use of the renminbi → Higher international demand for the renminbi → Some support for the exchange rate；But if the interest rate differential remains negative → Carry-trade capital flows reverse → Short-term depreciation pressure persists
notes: What is the China-U.S. interest rate differential? It is the difference between Chinese and U.S. government bond yields. A negative differential means Chinese yields are lower than U.S. yields, which has historically attracted capital into dollar-denominated assets.

Why can a widening interest rate differential still benefit the renminbi? Because the renminbi, with its low funding costs, can serve as a funding currency for carry trades. Offshore institutions borrow renminbi and convert it into dollars to invest, and this process itself requires buying renminbi first.

What is an asset absorption framework? It means providing investment outlets for renminbi held offshore, such as renminbi-denominated bonds, stocks, and wealth management products; otherwise, holders of renminbi have no choice but to convert it back into dollars.

Why is the hedging framework important? Offshore institutions holding renminbi assets are concerned about exchange rate fluctuations and need FX derivatives to hedge. Without sufficient market depth, they are reluctant to hold these assets for the long term.
Conditions for this logic to hold: the degree of capital account openness, returns on renminbi assets, and the stability of exchange rate expectations; all three are indispensable.

policy.title: Turkey’s foreign minister says Ankara weighing Saudi defense support, rules out offensive role
policy.raw_summary: Turkey, Pakistan and Saudi Arabia signed the Mecca Joint Defence Agreement, under which an armed attack on one member is considered an attack on all.

insight.what: 土耳其外长表示，安卡拉正评估沙特防务支持，同时排除进攻性角色，此前土耳其、巴基斯坦、沙特签署麦加联合防务协议。
insight.why: 市场原本认为中东防务格局由美国主导，这一协议意味着区域安全架构重组，可能影响中东资本流向和能源定价的风险溢价。
insight.chain: 三方防务协议签署 → 区域安全联盟重组 → 中东地缘风险溢价重新定价 → 原油供给预期波动 → 油价风险溢价上升 → 能源进口国通胀预期抬头 → 相关货币和债券承压
notes: 什么是地缘风险溢价？市场为'可能发生冲突'这件事额外要求的补偿，通常体现在油价、黄金、国防股上。
为什么防务协议影响油价？中东是全球原油主产区，联盟变化会改变市场对供应中断概率的判断。
为什么土耳其排除进攻性角色重要？这说明协议偏防御，降低了短期军事冲突概率，油价的风险溢价不会立刻飙升。
传导到资产：油价上行会推高全球通胀，进而影响各国央行的利率路径，最终反映在债券收益率和汇率上。

insight_en.what: Turkey's foreign minister said Ankara was assessing defense support for Saudi Arabia while ruling out an offensive role, following the signing of the Mecca Joint Defense Agreement by Turkey, Pakistan, and Saudi Arabia.
insight_en.why: The market had thought the Middle East's defense landscape was dominated by the United States. This agreement signals a restructuring of the regional security architecture that could affect capital flows in the Middle East and risk premiums in energy pricing.
insight_en.chain: Signing of the trilateral defense agreement → Restructuring of regional security alliances → Repricing of the Middle East geopolitical risk premium → Fluctuations in crude oil supply expectations → Higher oil price risk premium → Rising inflation expectations in energy-importing countries → Pressure on the relevant currencies and bonds
notes: What is a geopolitical risk premium? The additional compensation the market demands for the 'possibility of conflict,' usually reflected in oil prices, gold, and defense stocks.

Why does a defense agreement affect oil prices? The Middle East is a major global crude oil producing region, and changes in alliances alter the market's assessment of the probability of supply disruptions.

Why does Turkey's exclusion of an offensive role matter? It indicates that the agreement is primarily defensive, reducing the probability of near-term military conflict, so the risk premium in oil prices will not immediately surge.

Transmission to assets: higher oil prices push up global inflation, which in turn affects central banks' interest rate paths across countries and is ultimately reflected in bond yields and exchange rates.

tech.title: Nvidia-Backed Lumentum Sold Out of AI Server Parts Till 2029
tech.raw_summary: Lumentum Holdings Inc.’s optical components are “completely sold out” through early 2029 on demand from tech companies clamoring for faster AI data centers, according to its chief executive officer.

insight.what: 英伟达投资的Lumentum表示，其AI服务器用光组件已售罄至2029年初，因科技公司抢购更快的互联部件。
insight.why: 市场原本以为AI算力瓶颈在GPU，这条消息说明光互联已成为新的瓶颈，AI资本开支的受益环节从芯片扩展到光模块。
insight.chain: AI集群规模扩大 → GPU之间需要更快互联 → 光模块需求爆发 → Lumentum产能售罄至2029 → 光组件供不应求 → 价格与订单能见度上升 → 光模块与光通信板块盈利预期上修；同时供给瓶颈 → 云厂商资本开支被迫向光互联倾斜 → 算力部署节奏可能放缓
notes: 什么是光模块？AI服务器之间用光信号传输数据，光模块负责把电信号转成光信号，集群越大、互联越多，光模块需求越大。
为什么售罄至2029重要？这说明AI基础设施的投资不是短期脉冲，而是有长期订单支撑，改变了市场对AI资本开支可持续性的怀疑。
什么是资本开支？云厂商和科技公司花钱买服务器、建数据中心，这是AI产业链最上游的需求来源。
为什么光互联会成为瓶颈？GPU算力增长快，但把成千上万块GPU连起来需要极高带宽，光模块扩产周期长，跟不上GPU部署速度。
供给瓶颈的双面性：对光模块厂商是利好（订单饱满、议价力强），对云厂商是利空（部署变慢、成本上升）。

insight_en.what: Nvidia-backed Lumentum said its optical components for AI servers are already sold out until early 2029 as technology companies rush to buy faster interconnect components.
insight_en.why: The market had thought the bottleneck in AI computing capacity was GPUs. This news shows that optical interconnects have become the new bottleneck, expanding the segments benefiting from AI capital expenditure from chips to optical modules.
insight_en.chain: Larger AI clusters → Need for faster interconnects between GPUs → Surge in demand for optical modules → Lumentum's production capacity sold out until 2029 → Demand for optical components exceeds supply → Higher prices and greater order visibility → Upward revisions to earnings expectations for the optical module and optical communications sectors；At the same time, supply bottlenecks → Cloud providers forced to shift capital expenditure toward optical interconnects → Potential slowdown in the pace of computing capacity deployment
notes: What is an optical module? AI servers transmit data between one another using optical signals. Optical modules convert electrical signals into optical signals; the larger the clusters and the more interconnections, the greater the demand for optical modules.

Why does being sold out until 2029 matter? This shows that investment in AI infrastructure is not a short-term burst but is supported by long-term orders, changing the market's skeptical view of the sustainability of AI capital expenditure.

What is capital expenditure? It is the money cloud providers and technology companies spend on buying servers and building data centers. This is the most upstream source of demand in the AI value chain.

Why would optical interconnects become a bottleneck? GPU computing power is growing rapidly, but connecting thousands upon thousands of GPUs requires extremely high bandwidth. Optical module capacity expansion has long lead times and cannot keep pace with GPU deployment.
The two sides of supply bottlenecks: positive for optical module manufacturers (full order books and strong pricing power), but negative for cloud providers (slower deployment and higher costs).

tech.title: Franklin Templeton Sees Short-Term Debt as Sweet Spot for AI
tech.raw_summary: Franklin Templeton Chief Executive Officer Jenny Johnson said short-term debt issued by major technology companies offers investment opportunities in artificial intelligence, citing strong cash flows

insight.what: 富兰克林邓普顿CEO表示，大型科技公司发行的短期债券是AI投资的甜蜜点，兼具安全性和收益。
insight.why: 市场原本把AI投资等同于买科技股，这条观点把AI敞口扩展到短期信用债，改变了机构资金在AI主题上的配置结构。
insight.chain: AI资本开支扩大 → 科技巨头增加发债融资 → 短期公司债供给上升 → 机构资金从股票转向短债 → 科技股资金面承压 → 但短债收益率提供稳定回报 → AI融资成本被压低 → 资本开支可持续性增强
notes: 什么是短期债券？到期时间一年以内的债券，价格对利率变动不敏感，风险低，收益比货币基金高。
为什么叫甜蜜点？在利率高位时，短债既能锁定较高收益率，又不用担心长债那种价格大幅波动。
为什么科技巨头发短债？它们现金流强、信用评级高，发短债成本低，用来支持AI数据中心等资本开支。
传导到股票：如果机构资金转去买短债，科技股的边际买盘减少，估值扩张动力减弱。
这条逻辑的另一面：短债融资成本低，反而让科技巨头更容易维持高额资本开支，对AI产业链上游是利好。

insight_en.what: Franklin Templeton's CEO said short-term bonds issued by major technology companies are the sweet spot for AI investing, offering both safety and yield.
insight_en.why: The market had equated AI investing with buying technology stocks. This view extends AI exposure to short-dated credit, changing institutional investors' allocation mix within the AI theme.
insight_en.chain: Expansion of AI capital expenditure → Technology giants increase bond issuance to raise funds → Increased supply of short-term corporate bonds → Institutional capital shifts from equities to short-term bonds → Pressure on capital flows into technology stocks → But short-term bond yields provide stable returns → Lower AI financing costs → Greater sustainability of capital expenditure
notes: What are short-term bonds? They are bonds that mature within one year, have prices that are not very sensitive to interest rate changes, carry low risk, and offer higher returns than money market funds.

Why are they called the sweet spot? When interest rates are high, short-term bonds allow investors to lock in relatively high yields without worrying about the large price swings associated with long-term bonds.

Why do technology giants issue short-term bonds? They have strong cash flows and high credit ratings, so issuing short-term bonds is inexpensive for them, and they use the proceeds to support capital expenditure such as AI data centers.
Transmission to equities: if institutional capital shifts into short-term bonds, marginal buying demand for technology stocks decreases, weakening the impetus for valuation expansion.

The other side of this logic: low short-term bond financing costs actually make it easier for technology giants to sustain high capital expenditure, benefiting the upstream segments of the AI value chain.
